changes: Chronogram resolved: 'nobhranaya' read as nabho- (nabhas = 0) + nayana (2), with muni (7); read right to left this gives 720, not the two alternatives the first reading offered
Era set to 'unspecified' because the colophon names no era; NS assumed on palaeographic and historical grounds, giving ce_approx c. 1600
Title 'śrīvāstaka' normalized to Śrīvāstavya (the Kāyastha subcaste); note added that Hedayasiṃha probably stands for Hṛdayasiṃha

date.as_written: nobhranaya (!) munivarṣe māsasyaśrāvaṇastathā śitapakṣe tṛrodaśī (!) samāptaṃ kuca dinena

notes: The chronogram 'nobhranaya munivarṣe' is best read as nabho (0) + nayana (2) + muni (7). Read right to left, this gives 720. The colophon states no era. NS 720 (c. 1600 CE) is assumed because the manuscript is in Newari script; VS or ŚS 720 would be far too early. 'śrīvāṣṭaka' is a corruption of Śrīvāstavya/Śrīvāstava, a Kāyastha subcaste. 'kuca dina' stands for kujadina, i.e. Tuesday. The scribe's name 'Hedayasiṃha' (as in the catalogue) probably represents Hṛdayasiṃha. The tithi is śukla 13 (śitapakṣe = sitapakṣe). The weekday has not been verified against an ephemeris.
